takes.text: The air can't keep up with the ground.
It is pulled along only by friction, so for the first hours it is left behind.
The ground moves through it at about a thousand and forty miles an hour.
The strongest gust ever measured was about two hundred and fifty miles an hour.
This wind would be four times faster, blowing from the east, because the ground is running ahead of the air.
Winds like that would strip the surface, and they'd only be the beginning.
If you're enjoying this, tap like and follow.
And then the oceans start to move.
